overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the notices reflected what was reasonably anticipated 48 hours before the joint meeting, the public had no right to participate, and the minutes issue was a reminder only.

allegations.summary: Joint boards noticed an executive session on non-union contract negotiations but discussed the topic in open session without updating the notice.
allegations.key_passage: Following our review, we find that the Boards did not violate the Open Meeting Law because the posted meeting notices accurately reflected what was reasonably anticipated by the Boards 48 hours before the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the failure to update the notice denied the public an opportunity to participate in the forum for Ashby during the open-session discussion.
allegations.key_passage: the Boards were not required to allow any member of the public to participate in that discussion. See OML 2012-78; OML 2011-2.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the joint meeting did not clearly show whether a vote was taken to extend the Town Administrator's trial period; AG reminded the boards of recording requirements.
allegations.key_passage: Because there is no audio or video recording of the meeting, we are unsure whether such a vote did actually occur, but we remind the Boards that where votes are taken, this information must be included in the minutes.
